hints.title: Evaluating Bonus Eligibility
hints.text: An employee receives their entire salary as bonus if employee_id is odd and their name does not start with the character M.

hints.title: Formulating Conditional Output
hints.text: Use a case when expression checking employee_id % 2 = 1 and name not like "M%" to return salary, defaulting to 0.

hints.title: Ordering the Results
hints.text: Sort the output rows by employee_id ascending.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    employee_id,
    CASE
        WHEN employee_id % 2 = 1 AND name NOT LIKE 'M%' THEN salary
        ELSE 0
    END AS bonus
FROM Employees
ORDER BY employee_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) for ordering by employee_id
complexity.space: O(1) auxiliary space beyond result set
complexity.notes: Row-level conditional evaluation using CASE WHEN.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Separate union queries with order by are unnecessarily complex compared to declarative CASE WHEN.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Single table scan evaluates conditions inline.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should apply modulo arithmetic and pattern matching with LIKE correctly.
